title: Walking Robot Simulation
summary: A robot on an infinite XY-plane begins at (0, 0) facing north.
statement: A robot on an infinite XY-plane begins at (0, 0) facing north. It receives a sequence of commands: -2 for a left turn, -1 for a right turn, and 1 to 9 for moving forward a specified number of units. Some grid points are obstacles. If the robot encounters an obstacle, it stops moving but continues to the next command. The task is to find the largest squared Euclidean distance the robot travels. Note that an obstacle at (0, 0) does not prevent the robot from moving away from it, but it cannot return to (0, 0) due to the obstacle. Directions are defined as north (+Y), east (+X), south (-Y), and west (-X).
constraints: Robot begins at origin facing north; -2 turns left, -1 right, and positive commands move forward.
Stop before obstacles and return maximum squared distance reached.
hints: Movement must be simulated one unit at a time because an obstacle can stop a longer command early.
Track orientation and a hash set of blocked coordinates.
Rotate direction on negatives; for each forward unit test next coordinate before moving and update squared distance.
Every reachable intermediate position is considered, including the maximum before a later return toward the origin.
editorial: Every reachable intermediate position is considered, including the maximum before a later return toward the origin.

tests.explanation: The robot reaches (3,4), whose squared distance is 25.
The obstacle stops the eastward segment and the maximum squared distance is 65.
